one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: Checks 1–3 stay within their expect lines. Check 1 asserts only clamping behaviour: values inside, below, above, at the boundaries, lo===hi, and negative ranges. Check 2 asserts RangeError only for lo>hi. Check 3 has a fallback so a function documented without a heading still passes, and the stricter items sit under Advisory. Check 4 breaks the criterion. "npm test passes" only requires the command to succeed (exit 0), but the PASS condition also demands that "the summary shows `# fail 0`". That depends on exact output wording, which the expect line doesn't require. Node 22's `node --test` may use the spec reporter, which prints "ℹ fail 0" instead of "# fail 0", so a passing run could be marked as failing. This exact-output requirement belongs under Advisory, not in the PASS condition.

runs-as-written.why:
The criterion fails on the README check command, which appears in builder step 4 and verifier Check 3. Checks 1, 2 and 4 are valid as written.

The README command is wrapped in bash double quotes, and there `\\s` and `\\(` each become a single backslash: `\s` and `\(`. JavaScript then reads the string `'\s*\('` as plain `s*(` with no backslashes. That leaves `new RegExp('^#+s*`?'+k+'s*(','m')` with an unclosed group. It throws "SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: Unterminated group" for every export, so the command always fails, even on a correct PR. The verifier's fallback only covers a function that is documented without a heading; it does not cover the script crashing.

catches-traps.why: Item 1: the builder brief says "`subtract` is exported but NOT documented in README.md today, so it must be added too", and step 2 asks for `### subtract(a, b)` and `### clamp(x, lo, hi)` entries. Item 2: verifier Check 3 lists exported functions "(add, subtract, multiply, clamp, and any others)" and FAILs if "any exported function, e.g. `subtract` ... or `clamp`, has no description in README.md". It allows a function documented without a heading, but every function still needs an entry. Item 3: Check 2 calls clamp(5,10,0) and clamp(0,1,0.5), where lo is greater than hi, using `a.throws(..., RangeError)`, an instanceof check. It FAILs on "an error that is not a RangeError". All three items are handled.

avoids-must-not.why:
I checked the verifier brief against both must_not items.

1. Check 3 doesn't pass when subtract is undocumented. Its script loops over every function math.js exports, subtract included, and exits 1 if any is MISSING. The FAIL condition names `subtract` outright. The one fallback (a function described without a heading) still needs subtract "clearly described" in README.md, so the README layout isn't fixed either.

2. No condition is stricter than its line. Check 1 only tests clamp values inside, below, above and at the range edges, plus lo === hi. Check 2 needs only a RangeError, with no exact message and no parameter count. Check 4 needs exit 0 and no failing tests. The `# fail 0` wording is a little specific to the reporter, but it is just the normal summary from `node --test`, so it adds no real requirement. The lo === hi throw case and the test-file and README-wording items are marked advisory and are outside PASS/FAIL.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief against the verifier brief's checks. Step 4 of the builder brief has the builder run a `node -e "const fs=require('fs');const m=require('./math.js');const r=fs.readFileSync('README.md','utf8');const missing=...` script. It is the same, character for character, as the Check 3 probe in the verifier brief, down to the 'CHECK3 OK' output. That is a verifier probe leaking into the builder brief. It isn't the repository's own tests or a command named by an expect line (only `npm test` is). The builder's `assert.throws(() => clamp(5, 10, 0), RangeError)` test also matches one of Check 2's inputs. Telling the builder to write its own tests is allowed, though, so the Check 3 script alone is enough to fail the criterion. The rest of the builder brief (goal, context, implementation steps, `npm test`) is fine.
